author: NorthEast News Desk
body: A New Hampshire judge declared a mistrial Tuesday in the case of former youth detention center counselor Jeffrey Buskey after jurors heard testimony the court found they should not consider, according to The Associated Press.

Buskey, 60, of Litchfield, has pleaded not guilty to 21 counts of aggravated felonious sexual assault involving David Meehan, who was 14 when he arrived at the Youth Development Center in Manchester in 1995. The charges are allegations, and the mistrial did not resolve them.

Judge Will Delker initially instructed jurors to disregard testimony referring to alleged assaults by other staff. After a second reference, the judge ended the trial. Associate Attorney General Thomas Velardi said the state will evaluate its options, including trying the case again.

Buskey also faces separate charges involving three other former residents of the state-run facility, now called the Sununu Youth Services Center. The broader scandal has produced more than 1,100 civil lawsuits and a state settlement fund; those proceedings are separate from this criminal case.
dek: A judge ended Jeffrey Buskey’s trial after testimony referred to allegations involving other staff; prosecutors say they will consider whether to retry the case.
headline: Mistrial declared in New Hampshire YDC sexual-assault case
